_note: How the labs map to an Identity & Access Management (IAM) career path. Skill-area names follow the public outlines of each certification/platform; the mapping to labs is this project's own and describes simulated practice, not vendor training.

path.name: CompTIA Security+ (SY0-701)
path.why: The baseline security certification most IAM job postings ask for; covers identity, access control, zero trust and governance alongside the rest of security.

path.name: Microsoft SC-300: Identity and Access Administrator
path.why: Shows you can run identity in Microsoft Entra ID, the identity platform behind Microsoft 365 and Azure that most organisations use.

path.name: SailPoint identity governance (IdentityIQ / Identity Security Cloud)
path.why: SailPoint is a leading identity governance (IGA) product; employers that run it hire analysts and engineers who understand lifecycle, certifications and SoD.

areas.name: Implement and manage user identities
areas.plain: Create and manage users and groups, invite guests from other companies, and keep on-premises and cloud accounts in sync.

areas.name: Implement authentication and access management
areas.plain: Decide how people sign in (MFA, passwordless) and write the rules that allow, challenge or block a sign-in (Conditional Access, risk-based policies).

areas.name: Plan and implement workload identities
areas.plain: Govern the non-human identities: app registrations, service principals, managed identities and the permissions apps and automations get.

areas.name: Plan and automate identity governance
areas.plain: Keep access right over time: access packages, access reviews, just-in-time admin roles (PIM), and monitoring sign-in and audit logs.

areas.name: Identity lifecycle (joiner, mover, leaver)
areas.plain: Give new hires the right access on day one, adjust it when they change jobs, and remove all of it when they leave.

areas.name: Aggregation and correlation
areas.plain: Pull every account from every application and match each one to a person from the HR system; unmatched accounts are orphans.

areas.name: Roles, access profiles and entitlements
areas.plain: Bundle permissions into roles so access is granted by job, not one permission at a time.

areas.name: Access certifications (reviews)
areas.plain: Managers and owners regularly confirm or revoke each person's access, with evidence for auditors.

areas.name: Separation-of-duties (SoD) policies
areas.plain: Stop one person from holding two permissions that together allow fraud, such as creating and approving a payment.

areas.name: Provisioning, access requests and approvals
areas.plain: Grant and remove access through requests, approvals and automation instead of manual admin work.

areas.name: Audit evidence and reporting
areas.plain: Show auditors who had access, who approved it, and when it was removed.

areas.name: 4.6 Identity and access management
areas.plain: Provisioning, SSO and federation, access-control models, MFA, passwords and privileged access management.

areas.name: 1.2 Zero trust and AAA
areas.plain: Never trust by default: verify every request using identity, device and context.

areas.name: 5.1 Governance and data roles
areas.plain: Owners, custodians and policies that decide who may approve access.

areas.name: 4.7 Automation and orchestration
areas.plain: Automating provisioning and response safely, with guard rails and human approval.

job_search: Search the titles above plus the words SailPoint, Entra ID, Azure AD, Okta, CyberArk and access reviews; many IAM roles are hybrid or fully remote, which widens an Oklahoma search.

In Oklahoma, look at the state's central IT agency job board, large hospital systems, energy companies, banks and credit unions, aerospace and defense employers around Tinker Air Force Base, universities, and tribal nations and their enterprises, all of which run identity programs.
Read five real postings and copy their keywords into your resume and portfolio captions; match each keyword to a lab you can show.
Be explicit that portfolio work is a simulated lab with fictional data; interviewers value honest, well-explained practice over vague claims.
portfolio_guide: For each lab, capture four things: the work ticket (Lesson tab), the scenario run (Run the scenario tab), the case study page (Case study tab, Print / Save as PDF), and your practice score.
Screenshots: Windows Snipping Tool (Win+Shift+S) or macOS (Shift+Cmd+4). Screen recordings: Windows Game Bar (Win+G), macOS (Shift+Cmd+5) or the free OBS Studio.

Record a 60-90 second walkthrough per lab: the ticket and why it matters, run the scenario, point at two findings, say what you would fix, end with the lesson. Talk to the camera like you are briefing your team lead.
Publish the case-study Markdown files (python main.py case-study --all) in a GitHub repository with your screenshots, and post one lab a week on LinkedIn using the talking point.
Lead with the IAM labs (1, 2, 25, 26, then 5 and 8) when applying for identity roles.
